To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carbohydrate structures of wild-type and mutant VSV glycoproteins are similar, and that the altered polypeptides of tl-17 glycopeptide are deficient in sialic acid, but not in fucose, compared to wild-type VSV glycopeptide.

(1) the oligosacchardies of the glycoproteins of wild-type and mutant VSV are structurally similar and (2) the polypeptide composition of the glycopro-tein affects the extent of the addition of late-appearing oligosaccharidic components, sialic acid, and fucose.
the carbohydrate structures of the mutant glycoprotein are very similar to those of the wild-type glycoprotein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the structure of oligosaccharidic components of glycoproteins and their relationship to the structure of the polypeptide moiety.
the synthesis and structure of the glycoconjugates of VSV.
the structure, function and synthesis of the oligosaccaride units of the glycoproteins of VSV and of a thermolabile glycoprotein-deficient mutant of the virus, tl-17.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polypeptide of the glycoproteins of VSV and tl-17 is the determinant of the overall oligosaccharidic structure of the VSV glycoprotein.
the oligosacchride structure of the glycosylated polypeptide of VSV is determined by the structure of the polypeptide and not by any other factor.

the oligosaccharyltransferase, which is responsible for addition of the initial oligosaccharidyl unit to the nascent polypeptide, does not require a specific amino acid sequence in order to add the initial oligosacharyl unit to a polypeptide, but the subsequent processing of the carbohydrate moiety of the glycoproteins may be dependent upon the specific amino acid sequence of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the polypeptide backbone of the VSV glycoprotein does not determine the structure of the carbohydrate moeities, but rather the carbohydrate composition is determined by a series of enzymic reactions that occur in the Golgi apparatus.

the carbohydrate moieties of glycoproteins are determined to a large extent by the structure of the polypeptide backbone, and that the carbohydrate moeity is an important determinant of the biological activity of the polypeptides.
the oligosacchardie structure of the VSV glycoprotein is not significantly affected by changes in the polypeptide backbone.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the oligosaccharyltransferase is not responsible for the addition of sialylation and fucosylation to the VSV glycoprotein, and that there must be a separate enzyme that is involved in the addition of these two sugars to the glycoprotein.
the polypeptide backbone of the VSV glycoprotein does not determine the structure or the extent of the oligosacharide moieties.
the oligosacchride structures of the wt and mutant VSV glycoproteins are very similar.
